overview: A ridge gives the Cascades and Sierra a dry, foggy stretch, then a series of storms arrives from the Pacific from Sunday into midweek. The Sierra's Sunday system is weak, and the midweek storm is expected to be wetter and snowier than the one before.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Fog and cold start the weekend. A low offshore brings light showers from Saturday afternoon into Sunday, with snow levels around 2,500 feet. Stevens Pass is the top bet at 11 inches. Light snow mixing with rain follows Monday through Wednesday, with Mt. Baker at 15 inches.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Cold, foggy mornings Saturday, then a weak system brings light snow above about 4,000 feet Sunday. Monday is dry. A stronger storm arrives midweek, with forecasters less sure of its totals. Sugar Bowl leads at 13 inches. The NWS calls for 21 inches at Sugar Bowl from Sunday through Wednesday night.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Snow fades to flurries Sunday and Monday, then rain and showers take over midweek. Whistler is the best bet at 15 inches, mostly from Monday through Wednesday.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: A clear, bitterly cold night Saturday brings freezing fog to the Martis and Sierra valleys. A fast, weak storm brings light snow Sunday, enough to make the drive home hard in the evening. Monday afternoon through Tuesday evening is the best travel window. Mammoth gets 9 inches, with a stronger midweek system bringing more snow.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
